metadata.name: RAG Lab Evaluation Dataset
metadata.description: Test questions for measuring RAG performance across different difficulty levels

questions.query: What is vector search?
questions.ground_truth: Vector search uses dense numerical representations (embeddings) to find semantically similar documents using cosine similarity or other distance metrics.

questions.query: How does hybrid search improve retrieval?
questions.ground_truth: Hybrid search combines vector search (semantic) with BM25 (keyword) using Reciprocal Rank Fusion, achieving better recall by capturing both meaning and exact term matches.

questions.query: What is agentic chunking?
questions.ground_truth: Agentic chunking uses LLM analysis to create intelligent semantic boundaries in documents, respecting structure like headings, code blocks, and lists rather than using fixed-size chunks.

questions.query: Why use knowledge graphs in RAG?
questions.ground_truth: Knowledge graphs connect documents through wikilinks, tags, and folders, enabling multi-hop queries and discovering related documents that aren't semantically similar but are contextually connected.

questions.query: What are the trade-offs of LLM re-ranking?
questions.ground_truth: LLM re-ranking improves precision by 10-15% but adds ~2000ms latency and high compute cost. Best for critical queries with low QPS, not real-time systems.

questions.query: How does query expansion work?
questions.ground_truth: Query expansion adds synonyms and related terms to the original query, improving recall by ~5% with minimal latency cost (~10ms).

questions.query: What embedding model does this RAG system use?
questions.ground_truth: The system uses nomic-embed-text, a 768-dimensional embedding model that balances quality and speed.

questions.query: What document types can be uploaded to the system?
questions.ground_truth: The system supports PDF, Microsoft Office formats (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), Markdown, plain text, and RTF files up to 50MB.

questions.query: How many microservices are in the RAG Lab system?
questions.ground_truth: The system has 11 microservices: webapp, ingest, search, chat, docling, vector-db, embedding, knowledge-graph, reranker, api-gateway, and playwright-tests.

questions.query: What is the expected latency for hybrid search?
questions.ground_truth: Hybrid search (vector + BM25) typically takes ~100ms, with vector search at 20ms, BM25 at 15ms, and fusion at 10ms.

questions.query: How does BM25 differ from vector search?
questions.ground_truth: BM25 is statistical keyword matching based on term frequency, while vector search uses semantic embeddings to find meaning-based similarities. BM25 excels at exact matches, vector search at conceptual similarity.

questions.query: What is entity extraction used for?
questions.ground_truth: Entity extraction identifies key concepts, technologies, and proper nouns from documents, enriching metadata for better filtering and search.

questions.query: Which RAG features provide the best recall improvement?
questions.ground_truth: Hybrid search provides the largest recall boost at +20%, followed by agentic chunking (+15%), query expansion (+5%), and knowledge graph (+5% for multi-hop).

questions.query: How is precision different from recall?
questions.ground_truth: Precision measures what percentage of retrieved documents are relevant (accuracy), while recall measures what percentage of relevant documents were retrieved (completeness).

questions.query: What LLM models are available in the system?
questions.ground_truth: The system supports Llama 3.2 models in three sizes: 1B (fast), 3B (balanced), and 8B (accurate).

questions.query: What is Reciprocal Rank Fusion?
questions.ground_truth: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) is a method for combining ranked lists from multiple search methods, giving higher scores to documents that rank well across all methods.

questions.query: Why was this RAG system built with AI coding tools?
questions.ground_truth: The system was built with AI coding tools (Cursor/VS Code) to demonstrate modern development practices and show students what's possible with AI-assisted programming.

questions.query: What ports do the main services use?
questions.ground_truth: Main services use: webapp (5555), ingest (8001), search (8002), chat (8003), docling (8004), vector-db (8005), embedding (8006), knowledge-graph (8007), reranker (8008).

questions.query: How long does it take to rebuild the entire system from scratch?
questions.ground_truth: A complete rebuild from scratch takes approximately 50 seconds: 30 seconds for building and 20 seconds for service startup.

questions.query: What is the difference between faithfulness and answer relevance metrics?
questions.ground_truth: Faithfulness measures whether the answer is grounded in retrieved context (no hallucinations), while answer relevance measures whether the answer addresses the query (on-topic). An answer can be faithful but not relevant, or relevant but unfaithful.
